title: CutSign project file (.cutsign.json), versions 2, 3 and 4
description: The project document shared by the CLI writer (services/audit_project.py), the desktop writer and reader (apps/desktop editor-model.ts migrateProject, project-store.ts) and the Rust exporter (model.rs, export.rs). Versions 2 and 3 have the same shape; version 4 adds `preset` (required), `presentation`, `silenceThreshold`, `asset.role`, `segment.audio` and three origins (CREATOR_SELECTS F1a). The desktop upgrades 2 and 3 to 4 on open with preset `cctv`, which keeps every pre-v4 behaviour. A writer must emit every field listed in `required` of each object: the list is the union of what every reader needs, so a document that passes this schema opens in the desktop and exports in Rust. Cross references (segments[].assetId, sourceOrder, groups[].assetIds pointing at assets[].id) are NOT expressible here; tests check them separately.

id.description: Optional stable project identity, a UUID (REALTIME_AGENT_EDITING_MCP M1b). The desktop session assigns one to a project that has none and writes it with the next autosave; it never rewrites a file the user opened. It survives edits and restarts and changes only when a new project is created. The CLI writer does not emit it; Rust and the engine ignore it.

version.description: Document version. Readers reject any other value that carries `assets` with the error `[project.version_unsupported] Project version {n} was saved by a newer CutSign. Update the app to open it.` A document without `assets` is the version 1 analysis payload (analysis.v1.schema.json).

preset.description: Which analysis signals run and whether people lock footage. `cctv` keeps every pre-v4 behaviour; readers of v2/v3 documents default to `cctv`. Required from version 4 on (the `if`/`then` above), absent in version 2 and 3 documents. Rust and the engine validate it but do not act on it yet.

levelDb.description: Audio below this level in dBFS counts as silence.

seconds.description: Shortest quiet stretch that becomes a silence segment.

silenceThreshold.description: Optional (version 4): the per-project silence threshold of preset `creator` (CREATOR_SELECTS feature D7). Absent means the engine default; v2/v3 documents never carry it. Rust and the engine validate it but do not read it yet.

createdAt.description: When the project was first created. Required by the desktop type; the Rust exporter ignores it.

reviewedAt.description: Last time a human edited a review decision. Written by the desktop only.

assets.description: Every source video in the project, in import order. Required by the exporter.

sourceOrder.description: Asset ids in sequence order. The exporter walks this list and skips ids without an asset.

manualOrder.description: True once the user reordered sources by hand; the desktop then stops sorting by capture time. Absent means false.

segments.description: Edit segments over source time. Required by the exporter.

groups.description: Media pool groups. Optional: the desktop rebuilds every group whose pinnedMembership is false on open, so only pinned groups survive a round trip unchanged.

preprocessingRuns.description: History of preprocessing runs (CLI --pre and desktop Auto cut). Informational; no reader acts on it.

timestamp.description: Loose ISO-8601 date-time: Python isoformat() with offset and JavaScript toISOString() both match. Not `format: date-time` because strict ajv rejects unknown formats without ajv-formats.

timebase.description: Rational seconds per pts unit. The exporter rejects non-positive values at export time; the CLI and the desktop write 1/1000.

modifiedNs.description: File modification time in nanoseconds (Python st_mtime_ns). JavaScript numbers hold it only to about 2^53, so a desktop round trip may round the last digits.

sourceFingerprint.description: Size and mtime used to detect a replaced source and to key caches.

id.description: `asset-` + FNV-1a 32-bit hash (UTF-16 code units, base 36) of the lower-cased path with `/` separators. fixtures/asset-id.json pins the hash for the desktop and the CLI.

path.description: Absolute path of the source video. Required by the exporter.

name.description: File name shown in the media pool. Required by the desktop.

capturedAt.description: Capture time used for chronological ordering and date groups.

capturedAtSource.description: Where capturedAt came from. The engine writes embedded, filename or filesystem; the desktop adds import-order (queued, not probed yet) and manual.

importOrder.description: Stable tie-breaker when two assets share a capture time.

durationPts.description: Duration in timebase units; 0 while queued. Required by the exporter.

status.description: Analysis state. The exporter only renders assets whose status is ready.

error.description: Human readable reason when status is error. Desktop only.

relativeSourceFolder.description: Parent folder relative to the input root (`.` for the root itself). The CLI always writes it; the desktop fills it from probe and uses it for folder groups.

cameraLabel.description: Optional camera name; no writer emits it yet.

role.description: Optional (version 4): what the source carries in a creator project. No writer emits it yet; absent means camera.

width.description: Frame width from the import probe. Desktop only (PROPERTY_PANE P1); absent in older projects and in CLI output.

height.description: Frame height from the import probe. Desktop only, optional.

fps.description: Frame rate from the import probe. Desktop only, optional.

minCutSeconds.description: Engine min_cut_seconds at the last analysis. Desktop only (PROPERTY_PANE P2 / SEGMENT_SMOOTHING S3); absent in CLI output and in older projects.

id.description: Unique within the project. Required by the desktop; the exporter ignores it.

assetId.description: Owning asset. Must match an assets[].id (not checkable by this schema).

sourceOutPts.description: Exclusive end. The exporter drops a piece whose end is not after its start or runs past the asset duration.

included.description: Whether the segment is in the output. The exporter keeps only included segments.

origin.description: Who proposed the segment. human-protected means a person was detected; every reader MUST treat it as locked regardless of `locked`. silence, speech and loud (version 4) come from the audio analysis of preset `creator` and never lock.

review.description: Human review state. The exporter refuses a project with any pending segment.

locked.description: Optional, default false. Every reader MUST also treat origin == human-protected as locked. The CLI writes it explicitly; the desktop sets it on open; the exporter ORs it with the origin check.

label.description: Short human label (for example `Bright · pending cut`). The CLI writes it on every segment.

audio.description: Optional (version 4). Quietest level for `silence`, peak level for `loud`; absent for other origins. The renderer builds the card text from origin and this number, never from `label`.

source.description: Optional (version 4, AGENT_CHAT_EDIT D7'). Set on a proposal the in-app Assistant made from a review comment (origin `ai`, review `pending` until decided) and kept after the decision; the card shows it as a chip. `label` then holds the reason code. The exporter and the engine ignore it.

comment.description: The review comment the proposal came from, cut to 500 characters.

index.description: 0-based position of the comment in what the user pasted.

measurements.description: Numbers the card's reason line is built from (shake variance and threshold in px, scene time in s).

proposalSource.description: Provenance of an Assistant proposal (AGENT_CHAT_EDIT D7'): who asked, in which comment, through which model.

kind.description: How the group was formed. folder-date is written by the CLI (one group per folder and local day).

pinnedMembership.description: True for groups the desktop must keep as-is (manual sections). Groups with false are rebuilt from groupingConfig on open.

mode.description: Automatic grouping rule. The desktop offers date, folder, session and filename; the CLI writes folder-date, which the desktop groups like date.

timezone.description: IANA zone used to cut local days.

sessionGapMinutes.description: Desktop session grouping gap; the desktop writes 30 when absent.

status.description: Per-asset render outcome. `ready` appears when the CLI has no render record for an analysed asset and falls back to the asset status (build_audit_project).

output.description: Rendered review file, or null when nothing was written.

settingsSnapshot.description: Free-form copy of the settings the run used, kept for audit. Deliberately open: CLI and desktop snapshot different settings.

status.description: Run outcome. The CLI writes completed or completed-with-errors; the desktop also writes cancelled.

editor.description: Last editor view. Optional; the desktop opens in sequence mode when absent.

overlay.description: One burn-in overlay. Only the switch is defined in version 4; position, format and clock source arrive as optional fields with the round that renders them (contracts README rule 1: an optional field every reader can ignore is not a bump).

gapCaption.description: Show the time gap (for example `+12 min`) during the dip.

joint.description: How the output joins after one segment. Absent joints are plain cuts.

id.description: Optional (AGENT_CHAT_EDIT A2b). Every note the desktop writes has one (`note-<seed>`, repeatable on redo), so a later edit can name it.

source.description: Optional: set when the Assistant wrote the note.

assetRef.description: Optional (OVERLAY_CHANNEL O2b, D20): the id of a shelf asset attached to the note (`fluent/1f602`, `mine/<12 hex>`). A brief copies its file next to the anchor; an id no longer on the shelf is skipped. The exporter and the engine do not read it.

note.description: Reviewer note at a source time; also the source of soft subtitles.

rect.description: Box as fractions of the frame: a redaction's rect and an image overlay clip's placement (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D21).

id.description: Optional (AGENT_CHAT_EDIT A3a). Every box the desktop writes has one (`redaction-<seed>`, repeatable on redo), so a later edit can name it.

source.description: Optional: set when the Assistant asked for the box.

needsPlacement.description: Optional (AGENT_CHAT_EDIT D10): true while the box sits at its default place and nobody has moved it onto what it must hide. Every export refuses while one is true (desktop and backend).

redaction.description: Static redaction box over a source time range, burned into the export (AGENT_CHAT_EDIT D29).

oneOf.description: Glued to the footage of one clip: starts at `pts` in the clip's timebase. A cut inside the range cuts the overlay with it (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D7 b).

outputMapHash.description: sha256 of the output map pieces that start before `endSec`, at import (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D7). Another hash now means the clip is out of date.

oneOf.description: Seconds of the output video, for a clip that spans a joint. Valid while the output map up to `endSec` is the one it was imported on.

file.description: Absolute path of the alpha video, or of a still image of the shelf (`kind: image`), like `assets[].path`. Referenced, never copied (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D8).

label.description: Optional: the manifest's label, else the file name.

fromNoteId.description: Optional: the note the brief anchor came from.

briefRevision.description: The project revision the manifest names; 0 for a shelf sticker (`kind: image`), which has no brief (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D21).

fileHash.description: sha256 of the file at import; the export checks it again (D8′).

fileStat.description: Optional: size and modification time at import, the fast "file changed" check (D8′).

acceptedMapHash.description: Optional (D7′): the output map hash a person chose to use the clip on although it is out of date.

manifestId.description: Optional: `clips[].id` of the manifest, so importing it again replaces this clip.

kind.description: Optional (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D21): `image` is a still PNG / WebP placed from the shelf; absent means `video`, the full-frame alpha video of O2.

assetRef.description: Optional (D21): the shelf asset id the image came from (same pattern as `note.assetRef`). The preview loads it by id; the export reads `file`.

placement.description: Optional (D21): where an image clip sits, as fractions of the frame. Absent means the clip covers the frame (D4).

overlayClip.description: One alpha video, or one still image of the shelf, laid over the output (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D5, D21). Whether it is still in step with the timeline is derived, never stored (D7′).

overlayClips.description: Optional (OVERLAY_CHANNEL O2): imported alpha videos. Not the burn-in switches of `overlays`.

encodeAcknowledged.description: Optional (OVERLAY_CHANNEL D11): the person has seen once that boxes and overlays make the export re-encode.

audio.description: Output audio treatment; absent means original.

look.description: Declared picture adjustment; null means untouched. Its fields arrive with the round that renders it, and the export audit must then record it as enhanced.

presentation.description: Optional (version 4): how the output is presented (BASIC_EDITING research section 3.6). Every field may be absent or empty. The exporter reads `redactions` (burned in, AGENT_CHAT_EDIT D29) and `notes` (edit list comments, D30) and reads past the rest; the engine ignores it.
